question: India's first Olympic Values Education Programme (OVEP) was launched in __ __ .
solution:
The correct answer is__** Option 3.**__** **

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• ** The Indian Olympic Association (IOA) launched India's first Olympic Values Education Programme (OVEP)** in **Odisha** in **September** **2019**.
 
• The programme is aimed at inculcating values of **Olympism and Olympic education** in school-going children across the country.
 
• The programme was launched in collaboration with the **International Olympic Committee (IOC)** and the **United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF)**, and was initially implemented in** 100 schools in Odisha**. The programme has since been expanded to other states in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Odisha **is a state located in the eastern part of India. It is also known as **Orissa.**

 
 
• The state capital of Odisha is **Bhubaneswar, **and the largest city is **Cuttack.**
 
• Odisha has a rich cultural heritage and is known for its classical dance form, **Odissi,** and its ancient temples, including the famous **Jagannath Temple in Puri.**
 
• The state has a diverse geography that includes** coastal plains, forests, and hills**.
 
• **Odisha's economy** is largely based on agriculture, with major crops including** rice, sugarcane, and pulses**. The state also has significant mineral resources, including coal and iron ore.
 
 
 
• **Punjab** is a state located in the northern part of India.
 
 
• It is bordered by the Indian states of **Jammu and Kashmir to the north, Himachal Pradesh to the northeast, Haryana to the south and southeast, Rajasthan to the southwest, and the Pakistani province of Punjab to the west.**
 
• The capital city of Punjab is** Chandigarh**, which is a union territory and also serves as the capital of **Haryana.**
 
• **Punjab** is known for its** rich cultural heritage, including traditional music and dance forms like Bhangra and Giddha,** as well as its delicious cuisine which includes dishes like** Sarson ka Saag and Makki di Roti. The state is also known for its agricultural production, particularly in the cultivation of wheat and rice.**
 
• **The Sikh religion, which originated in Punjab**, is a major part of the state's culture and identity. The famous** Golden Temple,** located in the city of Amritsar, is one of the most important religious sites for Sikhs and is visited by millions of people every year.
 
 
 
• 
 
**Haryana** is a state located in **northern India**. It was carved out of the former state of **East Punjab on 1st November 1966.**

 
 
• 
 
The state is bordered by the states of **Punjab and Himachal Pradesh to the north, Rajasthan to the west and south, and Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand to the east.**

 
 
• 
 
**Chandigarh is the capital of both Haryana and Punjab,** and is a union territory administered by the central government. The major cities of Haryana include **Gurgaon (now known as Gurugram), Faridabad, Ambala, Hisar, Panipat, Karnal, Rohtak, and Panchkula.**

 
 
• **The economy of Haryana is largely driven by agriculture,** with the state being one of the largest producers of **wheat, rice, and sugarcane in the country.** It also has a rapidly growing industrial sector, with major industries including automobile** manufacturing, textiles, and information technology. Haryana is also known for its sportspersons, especially in the field of wrestling.**
 
 
 
• 
 
**Uttar Pradesh** is a state located in the **northern part of India**.

 
 
• 
 
It is the most populous state in India, with a population of over 200 million people.

 
 
• 
 
The capital of Uttar Pradesh is** Lucknow,** and other major cities include **Kanpur, Varanasi, Agra, and Allahabad.Uttar Pradesh has a rich history and is known for its cultural and religious diversity.**

 
 
• 
 
It is home to many important **Hindu, Buddhist, and Muslim pilgrimage sites, including the cities of Varanasi, Ayodhya, and Mathura**.The economy of** Uttar Pradesh** is mainly based on agriculture, but the state also has a growing industrial sector.

 
 
• 
 
Some of the major industries in the state include textiles, sugar, and leather. Uttar Pradesh is also known for its **handicrafts, including pottery, embroidery, and wood carving.**​
